findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
TvMainActivity and the launcher aliases are normal entry points; SessionForkConfirmation requires user confirmation. However the exported MainActivity aliases accept an explicit intent with a glance-action data URI plus extras and start a VPN connection to a recent entry without user interaction. Whether letting any app change the VPN connection counts as sensitive is a human call. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.
app/src/main/java/com/protonvpn/android/redesign/app/ui/MainActivity.kt:325: Exported activity routes any intent with the glance-action scheme to the widget action handler.
app/src/main/java/com/protonvpn/android/widget/WidgetActionHandler.kt:72: Handler connects the VPN based on intent extras.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0212: Use of Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys in Code
findings.explanation:
A hardcoded secret string is used as the HMAC-SHA256 key that authenticates UDP/TCP ping packets sent to VPN servers; anyone extracting it from the APK can forge authenticated pings.
app/src/main/java/com/protonvpn/android/vpn/ServerPing.kt:48: HMAC key hardcoded as a string constant.
app/src/main/java/com/protonvpn/android/vpn/ServerPing.kt:60: The constant is turned into the HMAC key used to sign ping data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0318: References to SDK APIs Known to Handle Sensitive User Data
findings.explanation:
The app passes a persistent installation ID to the Sentry SDK as the user ID (crash reporting is on by default, opt-out). This identifier must be declared in the Data safety form.
app/src/main/java/com/protonvpn/android/utils/SentryIntegration.kt:98: Installation ID sent to Sentry as the user identifier.

findings.title: MASWE-0072: Inadequate Privacy Policy
findings.explanation:
Ward found no privacy policy link or text in the scanned files. Google Play requires every app to have a privacy policy link or text inside the app, as well as in Play Console (rule checked 2026-11-23, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10144311).
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:42: The app's manifest: no privacy policy link anywhere in the app.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0225: Usage of Insecure APK Signature Key Size
findings.explanation:
Key size can only be read from the signed APK. Note: the release build type in source is signed with signingConfigs.debug (androiddebugkey); confirm that production builds are re-signed with the real release key.
app/build.gradle:338: Release build type uses the debug signing config.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0216: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
release_tests/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:24: android:allowBackup="true"
